candidates.locator: Page 7, Section body, table header row
candidates.exact_span:
Ambient       Effluent         Acute         Domestic       Chronic        Human        Domestic      Irrigation     Wildlife      Aquatic       Aquatic     Health     TMDL
                                       Conc          Conc.          Aquatic           Supply     Aquatic         Health       Criteria      Criteria      Criteria      Criteria      Criteria    Criteria
candidates.computation_change_reason: The table defines multiple parallel criteria columns (domestic supply, chronic/acute aquatic, human health, irrigation, wildlife, TMDL). Which column is selected as the operative water quality standard changes the Cs value used to derive enforceable effluent limits and compliance comparisons.

candidates.locator: Page 7, Section body, table column MQL
candidates.computation_change_reason: Method quantitation limits govern whether reported measurements are numerically comparable to criteria. Different readings of MQL applicability (enforceable floor, reporting threshold, or non-operative metadata) change whether a measurement can be compared to a limit (Purpose A) and how sub-MQL or absent results are classified (Purpose C).

candidates.locator: Page 7, Section body, table row Diazinon
candidates.computation_change_reason: This row lacks an MQL value while neighboring pesticide rows include one, and it mixes numeric criteria with 1E+100 placeholders and N/A for TMDL. Interpretation affects whether Diazinon measurements have an established comparison threshold and how missing or non-detect results should be treated.

Repeated 1E+100 entries in criteria columns may be read as effectively non-limiting, placeholder, or missing data. That choice changes which criterion is treated as binding when selecting the most stringent applicable standard.

candidates.locator: Page 7, Section body, table column Need TMDL
candidates.computation_change_reason: Whether N/A in the Need TMDL column means no TMDL-driven limit applies, TMDL status is undetermined, or a separate TMDL obligation exists changes effluent-limit derivation and whether additional TMDL-related monitoring or limits are in scope.

candidates.exact_span: No limits are established if the receiving stream is not designated for the particular uses.
candidates.computation_change_reason: Use-designation scope determines whether any numeric effluent limit is established for a parameter. A different reading of designated uses changes limit applicability (A), whether compliance-oriented monitoring is required versus report-only (B), and whether absent results reflect no applicable limit versus missing evidence (C).

candidates.exact_span: No limits are established if the potential instream waste concentrations are less than the chronic water quality criteria.
candidates.computation_change_reason: This exemption condition turns on how instream waste concentration is calculated and compared to chronic criteria. Different interpretations of the comparison or of 'potential' concentration change whether an enforceable limit is established and whether missing measurements should be treated as non-violative or unresolved.

candidates.exact_span: The most applicable stringent criteria are used to establish effluent limitations for a given parameter.
candidates.computation_change_reason: The rule for selecting among multiple criteria columns (most applicable versus most stringent, and how ties or non-applicable columns are handled) directly determines which numeric limit is enforceable for each parameter.

candidates.exact_span: Water quality criteria apply at the end-of-pipe for acute aquatic life criteria and discharges to public lakes.
candidates.computation_change_reason: The locus of application (end-of-pipe versus instream mixing zone) changes whether acute aquatic criteria and lake-discharge criteria govern effluent limits, altering the computed allowable concentrations.

candidates.exact_span: If background concentration exceeds the water quality criteria, water quality criteria apply. And "Need TMDL" shown to the next column of Avg. Mass
candidates.computation_change_reason: The background-exceedance trigger and the truncated TMDL cross-reference are ambiguous about when criteria still bind and when TMDL development or related obligations apply, affecting both the derived limit and downstream monitoring or implementation requirements.

This conversion factor links daily maximum and monthly average limits. Whether it is mandatory, default, or context-specific changes which reported monitoring period (daily versus monthly) is compared to which enforceable limit.

candidates.locator: Page 7, Section body, Applicable Water Quality-Based Limits
candidates.exact_span: Daily Max. Conc. = Cs + (Cs - Ca)(F*Qa/Qe)                             Monthly Avg. Conc. = Daily Max. Conc. / 1.5
candidates.computation_change_reason: These formulas are the operative mechanism for translating water quality standards into effluent concentration limits. Any different reading of formula structure, variable binding, or the repeated 1.5 divisor changes computed daily and monthly enforceable limits.

candidates.locator: Page 7, Section body, Applicable Water Quality-Based Limits, Where clause
candidates.exact_span: F   = Fraction of stream allowed for mixing (1.0 is assigned to domestic water supply and human health uses)
candidates.computation_change_reason: The assigned mixing fraction F varies by use type. Misclassification of which use category applies, or whether F=1.0 is automatic versus conditional, changes the calculated allowable effluent concentration.

candidates.locator: Page 7, Section body, Applicable Water Quality-Based Limits, Where clause
candidates.exact_span: Qa = Criteria Low flow (4Q3) or Harmonic Mean flow for Human Health Criteria
candidates.computation_change_reason: Selection between 4Q3 low flow and harmonic mean flow for Qa changes the dilution/mixing term in the limit formula and therefore the enforceable effluent concentration, especially for human-health-driven limits.

candidates.locator: Page 7, Section body, Applicable Water Quality-Based Limits, Where clause
candidates.exact_span:
Cs = Applicable water quality standard
                     Ca = Ambient stream concentration
candidates.computation_change_reason: Cs and Ca must be matched to the correct criteria column and ambient measurement. Ambiguity in which standard or ambient value is 'applicable' propagates directly into the derived effluent limit.

candidates.locator: Page 7, Section body, table formula column header
candidates.computation_change_reason: The acute aquatic instream waste concentration formula ties effluent concentration Ce to instream concentration via a fixed multiplier. Interpretation of when this column governs versus the chronic/domestic formulas changes the instream comparison used in Step 3 limit-establishment tests.
